title: Territory Fallback Orchestrator with Latency SLA Hedging and Capacity-Weighted Allocation
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Design and implement a Territory Fallback Orchestrator: a routing controller that prioritizes serving requests from the lowest-latency region while respecting regional capacity budgets and SLO budgets. The orchestrator combines three signals: latency SLA hedging (percentile-driven hedging when p95/p99 exceeds thresholds), territory affinity (soft territory affinity windows to preserve UX while allowing spillover), and capacity-weighted allocation (using realtime capacity hints from per-region schedulers). The goal is to reduce cross-region latency violations and avoid hard thrashing between regions during hot spikes by providing a graded fallback path and circuit gates that trigger graded shedding. This ticket covers design, simulation, implementation of the control loop, and a canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New router accepts per-request territory affinity metadata and capacity hints. 2) Under synthetic stress, p95 tail violations reduce by >=30% compared to current baseline without increasing token count by >10%. 3) Circuit gate transitions (closed->degraded->open) behave predictably in synthetic failure scenarios and documented in runbook. 4) Canaries show zero customer-facing 5xx increase and latency SLOs are maintained for Tier-1 customers. 5) Console dashboard exposes region-level capacity credits, hedging events, and per-route fallback counts.
design_notes: Core idea: maintain an AffinityScore = alpha * locality_preference + beta * (1 - latency_normalized) + gamma * capacity_margin. Locality_preference decays over time (soft territory affinity) to allow graceful spillover. Latency_normalized uses rolling p50/p95 windows per region. Capacity_margin comes from token-like credits emitted by regional schedulers (credits proportional to idle GPUs / planned throughput). Circuit gates are modeled as three-state (Closed/Degraded/Open) per region-route: Closed -> normal routing, Degraded -> probabilistic shedding and increased hedging to nearby regions, Open -> no new traffic except emergency flows. Shedding is graded by token class: background/low-priority flows shed first; API key tiers preserved until necessary. We will expose config knobs: hedging_percentiles, affinity_decay_seconds, capacity_credit_thresholds, shedding_order, circuit_open_thresholds.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype controller in alpha mode that reads existing region metrics (latency histograms, in-flight counts, capacity credits) and emits routing weights. 2) Run offline simulation using last 14 days of traffic to tune alpha/beta/gamma. 3) Implement deterministic switch in Router for territory affinity header + weight table. 4) Add circuit gate state machine and a bounded shedding queue with exponential backoff for retries. 5) End-to-end tests + chaos tests simulating region outage and bursty traffic. 6) Canary rollout to 1% of traffic for 48 hours with automatic rollback on SLO regression.
test_plan: - Offline replay: sweep alpha/beta/gamma and measure p95/p99 improvement and additional token usage. - Failure injection: region blackout, partial per-region throttling, and KV cache hotkey storm. - Load test: increase concurrent open connections to simulate burst and verify shedding order. - Metrics alerting: create temporary SLO rules for canary and verify rollback triggers. - Post-rollout synthetic checks for Tier-1 customers using 10 synthetic transactions per minute.
rollout_steps: 1) Feature flag gate + internal-only namespace rollout. 2) Canary to non-critical tenant set (1% traffic) for 48h. 3) Expand to 10% with enhanced observability for 72h. 4) Gradual ramp to 50% with automated circuit hysteresis checks. 5) Full rollout when all health signals are green for 7 days.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Oscillation between regions causing increased tail latency. Mitigation: Add hysteresis and dampening on weight changes; use decay windows and minimum steering intervals. Risk: Over-shedding premium customers. Mitigation: Tier-aware shedding with hard protection for API keys marked "tier:enterprise". Risk: Inaccurate capacity credits leading to misrouting. Mitigation: conservative defaults and cross-checks with regional autoscaler signals.
